newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Metals weigh on Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Metals weigh on Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market slid lower at the open on Tuesday after precious and base metals prices tumbled on offshore markets.
The golds led the way down with the gold index losing over two percent early, compared to a loss in the All Resources index of one percent and a loss in the market benchmark of just 0.44 percent.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index was 14 points lower at 2,371.1.

"The gold index has plunged again with the gold price off heavily overnight," said Derek Bond, director at Brisbane-based brokerage, Burrell and Co, who also suggested the stronger Australian dollar may still be encouraging selling from international investors.
"The strong Australian dollar may be causing some overseas selling as they start to lose out on the currency situation."
The Australian dollar hit a six year high just above US$0.8200 on Monday.
Bond pointed to the market's quick bounce off its early lows, saying the market looked to be steadying.
"The market probably saw the worst of the profit taking early and seems to be recovering a little bit as the morning progresses," he said.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to three, while about 37 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
